For `audit`, return exactly `safe,safety,terminates,liveness`. `safe` and `terminates` are booleans. `safety` is `null` when safe, otherwise `{"prefix":[edge IDs]}`, a finite walk from `start` ending at any unsafe state (empty allowed). `liveness` is `null` when terminating, otherwise `{"prefix":[edge IDs],"loop":[edge IDs]}`. The prefix starts at `start`; the nonempty loop starts at its endpoint and closes there. Repeating the loop must satisfy all declared fairness conditions, and every visited state in prefix and loop must be non-done. Prefixes/loops need not be shortest, simple, or canonical. At most 1000000 total edge IDs may occur in one response. Both predicates must be computed even if one fails. A whole-SCC fairness heuristic is insufficient: a fair nonterminal subcycle can exist in an SCC containing a strongly fair action whose only exits leave that SCC.

## Lossless TLA+ export

For `export`, return exactly `{"module":string,"config":string}`. `module` must be a parsable module named `ModelData`, with only the following eight constant definitions, in this order, following `EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets`: `Nodes,Initial,Edges,ActionNames,WFIds,SFIds,SafeNodes,DoneNodes`. Integers use decimal notation; sets use `{...}`; tuples use `<<...>>`; use no expressions, helper operators, comments, overrides, or other definitions except `Nodes == 0..(n-1)`, written as the concrete range such as `0..3`. Module header/footer are `---- MODULE ModelData ----` and `====`. Whitespace is arbitrary.

`ActionNames` is the tuple of all edge/fairness names sorted in ASCII order. Actions have 1-based tuple indices. `Edges` is the set of `<<source,action_index,target>>` triples for **all** input explicit edges. `WFIds` and `SFIds` contain the corresponding declared action indices. `SafeNodes` and `DoneNodes` contain exactly the state indices satisfying the predicates above. `Initial` is `start`. Sets can be in any order. Empty sets and the empty tuple are permitted. The implicit stutter is represented by the harness, not by adding to `Edges`.

`config` must contain exactly these tokens, with arbitrary whitespace: `SPECIFICATION Spec INVARIANT Safety PROPERTY Termination CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE`. The public image supplies Python, not Java or TLC. Export correctness is checked structurally against all input edges, predicates, and fairness declarations; running TLC is not required of the submission. A maintainer with a separately provisioned TLC installation can optionally save the module as `ModelData.tla` beside the provided immutable `/app/EPIC.tla` and run the supplied configuration. The harness toggles an auxiliary bit on every explicit edge, so explicit self-edges count as action occurrences under TLA+ fairness; implicit stutters do not. Deleting transitions, changing fairness, changing predicates, or replacing the harness cannot satisfy export correctness. The checker can validate the complete exported relation independently of your audit answer. Do not modify `/app/EPIC.tla`.

## Resources and verification

Each invocation receives at most 32 requests and 64 MiB total stdin. It runs with 1 CPU, 60 CPU seconds, 90 seconds wall time, 1024 MiB address space, 32 processes, 64 file descriptors, 64 MiB combined stdout/stderr, and a 64 MiB temporary-work allowance. Output may be at most 16 MiB per line. Use iterative graph traversal for deep graphs. No per-request startup penalty is scored. Agent development has 4 hours and 2 CPUs/2048 MiB/2048 MiB storage; runtime limits above are the separate submission limits. `python3 /app/check_examples.py` checks the small public examples. Hidden verification covers protocol loss/reorder/duplication and reuse, exact arithmetic/barriers, graph safety, mixed fairness with fair subcycles, valid noncanonical witnesses, lossless model export, malformed inputs, and bounded maximum-size cases. Any correct implementation and any valid witness satisfying this contract are accepted. This is a functional task, not a speed competition.

Sources: [EPIC paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18683v2), [official artifact](https://github.com/In-Net/EPIC/tree/b3dd05f8b75a02594e2ebdfb9e569c14d3ecb55d/verify), and [Lamport, Specifying Systems, chapters 8 and 14](https://lamport.azurewebsites.net/tla/book.html). The bounded star, JSON protocol, explicit graph contract, witness format, and TLA+ exporter are new adaptations. Upstream protocol source is not bundled.
